args.text:
Batch audit: 8 runs, all 8 accepted. 2 flagged, 6 cleared.

Flagged as summary outlier (2 runs): r01 and r06. Their largest flank difference is at 284 µm from the tip, while every other run has it at 1074 µm. That means the curvature-rate profile has a different shape. Both runs pass rigid invariance and closure. Their growth zone (684 µm against 695 µm) and centre REGR peak (52.96 %/h against 53.1 %/h) differ only a little, even though their z-scores are large.

Cleared (6 runs): r02, r03, r04, r05, r07 and r08. They pass rigid invariance and closure, and their REGR peak (421 µm), growth zone (695 µm) and flank-difference position (1074 µm) match the batch. In r04, r05 and r08 the largest width-free ratio is 0.074 against a batch median of -0.019. The z-score of 4.18 comes from a very small MAD; the actual difference is small and close to zero, so I don't count it as a fault.

What the flagged runs share: both report the width-free ratio, needed 6 steps, kept one remedy and had no roll-backs. All their summaries are identical, and they differ from the batch only in where the flank difference is largest.

Every run used the width-free ratio, so the plane-sections check was not run on any of them.

The summaries repeat in three identical groups: r01 and r06; r02, r03 and r07; r04, r05 and r08. Check whether these are really separate roots or time windows.
